questions.q: What is resource planning, and why is it essential in a country like India?

answer.text: Resource planning is the widely accepted strategy for the balanced and judicious use of resources. It involves identifying and surveying resources across regions, evolving a planning structure with the technology and skills to develop them, and matching resource development with overall national development plans.

Resources in India are very unevenly distributed. Some states such as Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh are rich in minerals and coal but poor in water and infrastructure, while Rajasthan is rich in solar and wind energy but short of water. A few regions are almost self-sufficient and some are acutely short of vital resources.

answer: Planning ensures that scarce resources are conserved and used sustainably for the needs of both present and future generations.

questions.q: Describe the major types of soils found in India.
answer: India has a wide variety of soils formed by differences in relief, climate and rock type.

Also called regur, formed from lava in the Deccan; it retains moisture well and is best suited to growing cotton.
Red soils develop on crystalline rocks in the Deccan and turn reddish from iron; laterite soils form in high-rainfall areas through leaching and support tea, coffee and cashew.
Arid soils are sandy and saline, found in Rajasthan, while forest soils occur in the hilly and mountainous regions.

questions.q: How do human activities cause land degradation in India, and what measures can restore land?

answer.text: under great pressure in India, and human activities degrade it in several regions.

list: Deforestation and overgrazing strip the land of cover and cause soil erosion
Mining leaves land scarred, and its dumps degrade nearby areas
Over-irrigation causes waterlogging and increases the salt content of the soil, while industrial waste pollutes it
Afforestation, proper grazing management and planting shelter belts check erosion
Controlling mining waste and treating industrial effluents, and stabilising sand dunes, help reclaim degraded land

questions.q: Why is soil conservation important, and what methods are used to conserve soil in different regions?

answer.text: takes thousands of years to form but can be lost quickly to erosion, so conserving it is essential for agriculture and life.

list: On hill slopes, contour ploughing and terrace farming slow the flow of water and reduce erosion
In dry regions, strips of grass and shelter belts of trees check the wind
Building bunds and check dams in gullies stops them from widening
Planting trees and rotating crops keep the soil fertile and bound together
